reason: The learning target is inferential reading and register judgment, not a spatial or dynamic process. Motion would add no semantic information: the evidence lives in the wording of three sentences and in the learner's own sentence production. A text-first treatment also matches the stated accessibility requirement and directly counters the misconception that more animation means better learning.
staticAlternative: Three short context cards with 'meticulous' highlighted and an annotation gutter for 'clue -> inference'; a three-point connotation continuum (dismissive / neutral / admiring) where the learner places the word for each context; a substitution test comparing meticulous with careful, fussy and pedantic to show why no single synonym captures register; and a sentence-writing prompt checked against a three-item rubric (context fit, connotation fit, hedge about register).
